summary: In August 1994, a translucent, gelatinous substance rained down six times over the small town of Oakville, Washington. Shortly after contact with the mystery rain, dozens of residents fell ill with severe flu-like symptoms and extreme vertigo, while several domestic pets died. Laboratory testing revealed the blobs contained intact biological cells and human-pathogenic bacteria, yet official investigations abruptly stalled and primary samples mysteriously vanished from state laboratories.
research_points: August 7, 1994 event timeline: Local resident Sunny Barclift and police officer David Lacey encounter sticky, jelly-like precipitation, followed within hours by severe respiratory illness and hospitalization.
Initial chemical analysis by the Washington State Department of Ecology, where technician Mike McDowell discovered human white blood cells and complex cellular structures within the blobs.
Secondary testing by AmTest Laboratories identifying two distinct bacteria species (Enterobacter cloacae and Pseudomonas fluorescens) capable of causing severe human infections.
The naval bomb testing hypothesis versus the biological weapon test hypothesis, spurred by local reports of unusual low-altitude military flight maneuvers prior to the drops.
The sudden disappearance of primary laboratory samples from state archives and the complete lack of an official final explanation by state authorities.
title: Gökyüzünden Yağan Zehirli Madde: 1994 Oakville Felaketi
description: 7 Ağustos 1994 sabahı Washington'ın küçük Oakville kasabasına yağmur yerine şeffaf ve yapışkan bir jöle yağmaya başladı. Bu garip maddeye dokunan kasabalılar saatler içinde ağır hastalıklara yakalandı, hayvanlar telef oldu. Laboratuvar incelemelerinde maddenin içinde canlı hücreler ve tehlikeli bakteriler bulundu. Peki bu madde neydi? Askeri bir biyolojik deney mi, yoksa açıklanamayan atmosferik bir felaket mi? Shadow Archive ile Oakville olayının karanlıkta kalan tüm arşiv belgelerini inceliyoruz.
